ei.title: How Slight Deviations from Dress Norms Are Judged
ei.subject: 9월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: How Slight Deviations from Dress Norms Are Judged

fullPassage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people (A)[avoid / prefer] clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having (B)[higher / lower] status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as (C)[negative / positive] because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) prefer=선호하다, (B) higher=더 높은, (C) positive=긍정적인
det.analysis:
✅ ① prefer — higher — positive: 원문 일치. 사람들은 기대에 맞는 옷을 선호하고(prefer), 규범을 살짝 어긴 사람을 더 높은(higher) 지위로 보며, 약간의 일탈을 긍정적(positive)으로 판단한다 ←정답
❌ ② avoid — higher — positive: (A) avoid(피하다)는 prefer(선호하다)의 반대
❌ ③ prefer — lower — positive: (B) lower(더 낮은)는 higher(더 높은)의 반의어
❌ ④ prefer — higher — negative: (C) negative(부정적인)는 positive(긍정적인)의 반의어
det.tip: people prefer clothing(선호) / higher status(더 높은 지위) / judge ... as positive(긍정적으로)

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that (A)[violates / matches] expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness (B)[increased / decreased] audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these (C)[major / slight] deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) matches=부합하다, (B) increased=높였다, (C) slight=약간의
det.analysis:
❌ ① violates — increased — slight: (A) violates(위반하다)는 matches(부합하다)와 반대
❌ ② matches — decreased — slight: (B) decreased(낮췄다)는 increased(높였다)의 반의어
❌ ③ matches — increased — major: (C) major(큰)는 slight(약간의)의 반의어
✅ ④ matches — increased — slight: 원문 일치. 기대에 부합하는(matches) 옷을 선호하고, 독특함이 평가를 높였으며(increased), 약간의(slight) 일탈이 긍정적으로 평가됨 ←정답
det.tip: clothing that matches expectations(부합) / increased ratings(높임) / slight deviations(약간의 일탈)

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one (A)[trivial / notable] exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that (B)[valuing / ignoring] uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is (C)[powerless / powerful] enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) notable=주목할 만한, (B) valuing=중시하는 것, (C) powerful=강력한
det.analysis:
❌ ① trivial — valuing — powerful: (A) trivial(사소한)은 notable(주목할 만한)의 반의어
✅ ② notable — valuing — powerful: 원문 일치. 하나의 주목할 만한(notable) 예외가 있고, 독특함을 중시하는 것(valuing)이 평가를 높이며, 개인이 대가를 감수할 만큼 강력하다(powerful) ←정답
❌ ③ notable — ignoring — powerful: (B) ignoring(무시하는 것)은 valuing(중시하는 것)과 반대
❌ ④ notable — valuing — powerless: (C) powerless(무력한)는 powerful(강력한)의 반의어
det.tip: one notable exception(주목할 예외) / valuing uniqueness(중시) / powerful enough to risk(강력한)

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people ①<u>prefer</u> clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one ②<u>notable</u> exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having ③<u>lower</u> status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as ④<u>positive</u> because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 규범을 살짝 어긴 남성은 '더 높은(higher)' 지위로 여겨졌다. lower(더 낮은)로 바꾸면 문맥 모순
det.analysis:
❌ ① prefer — 원문 일치. '기대에 맞는 옷을 선호한다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② notable — 원문 일치. '하나의 주목할 만한 예외'라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ lower — 원문은 higher(더 높은). 빨간 나비넥타이를 맨 남성은 '더 높은' 지위와 역량으로 평가받았으므로 lower(더 낮은)는 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ positive — 원문 일치. '약간의 일탈을 긍정적으로 판단한다'는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: higher status and competence(더 높은 지위와 역량). lower는 반의어라 부적절

A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who ②<u>followed</u> established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing ③<u>uniqueness</u> increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is ④<u>powerful</u> enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 연구는 규범을 살짝 '어긴(broke)' 사람들에 대한 반응을 다뤘다. followed(따른)로 바꾸면 일탈이 성립하지 않아 모순
det.analysis:
❌ ① investigate — 원문 일치. '이러한 판단을 조사하는 연구'라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② followed — 원문은 broke(어긴). 연구 대상은 규범을 '어긴' 사람들인데 followed(따른)로 바꾸면 일탈 자체가 없어져 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ uniqueness — 원문 일치. '독특함을 중시하는 것'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ powerful — 원문 일치. '대가를 감수할 만큼 강력한'이라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: people who broke established norms(규범을 어긴). followed는 문맥상 부적절

In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research ①<u>explored</u> observers' ②<u>reactions</u> to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that ③<u>valuing</u> uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is ④<u>powerless</u> enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 약간의 일탈은 개인이 대가를 감수할 만큼 '강력하다(powerful)'는 신호. powerless(무력한)는 정반대
det.analysis:
❌ ① explored — 원문 일치. '관찰자들의 반응을 탐구했다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② reactions — 원문 일치. '관찰자들의 반응'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ valuing — 원문 일치. '독특함을 중시하는 것'이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ powerless — 원문은 powerful(강력한). 일탈은 개인이 사회적 대가를 '감수할 만큼 강력하다'는 신호이므로 powerless(무력한)는 모순 ←정답
det.tip: powerful enough to risk the social costs(강력한). powerless는 반의어라 부적절

det.korean: expectations=기대. 사람들은 기대에 '부합하는' 옷차림을 선호한다
det.analysis:

det.analysis:
❌ ① traditions: traditions(전통)는 규범을 '벗어난' 것과 반대 개념
✅ ② deviations: 원문 일치. 'these slight ___ from the norm'에서 규범으로부터의 약간의 일탈이므로 deviations가 적절 ←정답
❌ ③ decorations: decorations(장식)는 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ donations: donations(기부)는 문맥과 무관

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 investigate와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: investigate=조사하다 → examine=조사하다/살펴보다
det.analysis:
✅ ① examine: examine(조사하다/살펴보다)은 investigate(조사하다)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ② ignore: ignore(무시하다)는 조사와 반대 의미
❌ ③ create: create(만들다)는 조사와 전혀 다른 의미
❌ ④ hide: hide(숨기다)는 조사와 무관
det.tip: investigate = examine = 조사하다, 살펴보다

❌ ① avoided: avoided(피했다)는 탐구와 반대 의미

❌ ③ tiny: tiny(아주 작은)는 크기와 관련된 다른 의미축

det.tip: one notable exception = remarkable(주목할 만한 예외). ordinary·common은 반의어 함정

det.analysis:
✅ ① major: major(큰/중대한)는 slight(약간의)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② minor: minor(작은/사소한)는 slight와 유사어
❌ ③ subtle: subtle(미묘한)도 slight와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ partial: partial(부분적인)은 크기·정도와 다른 의미축
det.tip: slight(약간의) ↔ major(큰). minor·subtle은 유사어 함정

questions.passage:
(A) The dinner was a formal <u>affair</u>, and every guest arrived in a black-tie outfit. Nobody wanted to look out of place at such an event.
(B) The newspaper reported on the political <u>affair</u> that forced the minister to resign. The scandal had been hidden from the public for months.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 affair의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: affair: (A) 행사·모임 (정장 차림의 공식 행사) / (B) 사건·스캔들 (장관을 사임하게 한 정치적 사건)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 사건·스캔들 — (B) 사건·스캔들: (A)는 정장 차림의 '행사·모임'이지 사건이 아님
✅ ② (A) 행사·모임 — (B) 사건·스캔들: (A) a formal affair는 '공식 행사', (B) the political affair는 '정치적 사건·스캔들' ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 행사·모임 — (B) 행사·모임: (B)에서 장관을 사임시킨 것은 '사건'이지 행사가 아님
❌ ④ (A) 사건·스캔들 — (B) 행사·모임: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
det.tip: affair: ① (모임) 행사 ② (사건) 스캔들 — 문맥에 따라 의미 구분. 본문의 a black-tie affair는 '행사'

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person or thing that is not included in a general statement or does not follow a rule"

det.korean: exception=예외 (일반적인 진술에 포함되지 않거나 규칙을 따르지 않는 사람/사물)
det.analysis:
❌ ① expectation: expectation(기대)은 앞으로 일어날 일에 대한 예상이지 예외가 아님
❌ ② extension: extension(연장/확장)은 정의와 무관
❌ ③ execution: execution(실행/처형)은 정의와 무관
✅ ④ exception: exception(예외)은 '일반 진술에 포함되지 않거나 규칙을 따르지 않는 것'이라는 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: exception = 예외. with one notable exception(하나의 주목할 만한 예외)

questions.passage: A series of studies __________ (publish) in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: publish(동사) → published. 'A series of studies ___ in an article'에서 연구가 '출판된' 것이므로 과거분사 published로 명사를 뒤에서 꾸며 줌
det.analysis: A series of studies __________ (publish) in an article — studies(연구들)는 사람이 출판하는 '대상'이므로 수동의 과거분사 published가 와서 'studies published in an article(어떤 글로 출판된 연구들)'처럼 명사를 뒤에서 수식. publish를 published로 변환
det.tip: studies published in an article: 과거분사(published)가 명사(studies)를 뒤에서 수식

questions.passage: The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough __________ (risk) the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: risk(동사) → to risk. '형용사 + enough' 뒤에는 to부정사가 오므로 to risk. '대가를 감수할 만큼 (충분히) 강력한'
det.analysis: powerful enough __________ (risk) — 'enough(충분히)'가 형용사 powerful 뒤에 오면 그 뒤에는 'to + 동사원형'이 이어진다. 따라서 risk를 to risk로 바꿔 'powerful enough to risk(감수할 만큼 강력한)'를 완성
det.tip: 형용사 + enough + to부정사: powerful enough to risk(감수할 만큼 강력한)

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that __________ — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: matches expectations=기대에 부합하다. 사람들은 기대에 부합하는 옷차림을 선호한다
det.analysis:
❌ ① breaks traditions: '전통을 깨는' 옷은 선호가 아니라 예외적 일탈에 해당
❌ ② hides emotions: '감정을 숨기는' 것은 옷차림-기대 맥락과 무관
✅ ③ matches expectations: 원문 일치. 'people prefer clothing that ___' 뒤에 surgeons in scrubs 같은 예시가 이어지므로 기대에 부합함이 적절 ←정답
❌ ④ follows others: '남을 따라 하는' 것은 기대 부합과 다른 표현
det.tip: clothing that matches expectations(기대에 부합하는 옷) — surgeons in scrubs가 그 예시

questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations — surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue — with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to __________ of such behaviors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: risk the social costs=사회적 대가를 감수하다. 개인이 그러한 행동의 사회적 대가를 감수할 만큼 강력함을 시사
det.analysis:
✅ ① risk the social costs: 원문 일치. 'powerful enough to ___ of such behaviors'에서 그러한 행동의 사회적 대가를 '감수'할 만큼 강력하다는 맥락에 적절 ←정답
❌ ② enjoy public benefits: '공적 이익을 누린다'는 대가를 감수한다는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ avoid all attention: '모든 주목을 피한다'는 눈에 띄는 일탈 맥락과 모순
❌ ④ follow strict rules: '엄격한 규칙을 따른다'는 규범을 어긴다는 내용과 반대
det.tip: powerful enough to risk the social costs(사회적 대가를 감수할 만큼 강력한)
